requirement:
For backends that accept explicit cache checkpoints, when the backend and model
support prompt caching, every provider request MUST place one cache checkpoint
after the system prompt of {cite}`requirements.authoring.prompt_parts` and
another at the end of its last message, so each request reuses the tool
definitions and system prompt that earlier assessments of its kind sent, and
the conversation its own earlier requests sent. Cache checkpoints MUST NOT
change the content of a request.

For OpenAI, which caches matching prompt prefixes automatically, the harness
MUST keep the system prompt and tool definitions unchanged across requests in
one conversation and replay prior conversation content in its original order.
It MUST NOT insert checkpoint blocks.
rationale:
I found no gaps. Each obligation has code that carries it out and a test that asserts its outcome.

**Bedrock, explicit checkpoints**
- **Backend and model support.** `src/authoring/providers.rs#impl[RigProvider]/fn[connect]` sets `caches` from `bedrock_caches`, which is true only for the Claude and Nova families. It is false for Ollama and OpenAI. The unit test `cache_checkpoints_are_requested_for_caching_models` covers this: Claude and Nova are accepted, Llama and a fixture model are rejected.
- **Every request gets checkpoints.** `src/authoring/providers.rs#impl[RigProvider/CompletionProvider]/fn[complete]` calls `place_cache_checkpoints` on every request when `caches` is set. That sets `request.options.cache = Some(CacheRetention::Short)`. The vendored `rig-bedrock` turns this into a checkpoint after the system prompt and one at the end of the last message. `fn[converse]` in `src/authoring/mod.rs` sends all requests through `complete`.
- **Two checkpoints, in the right places.** `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[claude_requests_carry_cache_checkpoints_and_record_cache_usage]` asserts these points on each request body:
  - A `cachePoint` follows the system text.
  - A `cachePoint` ends the last message.
  - There are exactly two `cachePoint` occurrences.
  - This also holds on a request that follows a reasoning turn.
- **Reuse of tools, system prompt and conversation.** `fn[converse]` sets the tools once and keeps the system prompt fixed through `prompt.request()`. It only appends to the chat history, so earlier content is a stable prefix. The system prompt comes from `prompt_parts`, which is cited and not reassessed here.
- **Checkpoints must not change content.** The unit test shows the request serializes identically to the original apart from the cache option. The integration test strips the checkpoints from the cached request bodies and finds them equal to the bodies sent to an uncached model.

**OpenAI**
- `connect` sets `caches` to false for OpenAI, so no checkpoint is requested.
- `fn[converse]` keeps the tools and system prompt fixed and appends to the history in order.
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[openai_responses_replays_tool_calls_and_records_usage]` asserts:
  - `instructions` and `tools` are identical across the two requests.
  - The second request's input starts with the first request's input unchanged, followed by the function call and its output in order.
  - No checkpoint keys or block types (`cachePoint`, `cache_control`, `cache_point`, `cache_checkpoint`) appear in any request body.

I found no unspecified behavior in the `{impl}` code, and no `{fixme}` references apply.

For OpenAI, which caches matching prompt prefixes automatically, the harness
MUST keep the system prompt and tool definitions unchanged across requests in

:::{req} prompt_parts
Each assessment conversation MUST send its prompt as a system prompt followed by
one user message, the subject message, filled from the first and second text
blocks of the prompt requirement for the assessment's kind. The kinds are
requirement, example, citation review, site review, and a verifier of each of
those. A system prompt MUST be the same for every assessment of its kind, so
every placeholder whose value depends on the subject MUST be in the subject
message.
